- Model tends to overestimate prices, especially in the early part of the forecast horizon (first 5–10 days).
- Overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., 70→76 range) — model peaks too high and then undercorrects.
- Underestimates in the final 5–10 days of forecast — shows mean reversion bias, failing to capture sustained upward momentum.
- Forecast lags behind true price movements by 1–3 days, particularly in the middle of the horizon.
- High variance in forecast confidence around mid-forecast period — model overreacts to short-term volatility.
- Model fails to capture long-term trend persistence — underestimates sustained upward momentum in 30-day windows.
- Overconfident in early forecast days — model often starts with high values that don’t align with true price behavior.
- Sensitive to recent price spikes — model reacts too strongly to recent highs, leading to overcorrection or overshoot.
- Underestimates price stability in low-volatility periods — fails to recognize when prices are consolidating or trending sideways.
- Model exhibits “sticky” behavior — tends to hold onto previous high forecasts even when new data suggests a correction.
